text_blocks.snippet: Jardiance (empagliflozin) is a medication that helps your kidneys remove excess sugar through your urine. Because of how it works, it can cause several common and serious side effects.

list.snippet: Increased urination: You will likely need to pee more often. Taking your dose in the morning can help prevent getting up during the night.
Urinary tract infections (UTIs): Symptoms include a burning sensation when you pee, an urgent or frequent need to go, cloudy or bloody urine, or lower back/side pain.
Genital yeast infections: These happen in both women (vaginal itching, burning, thick white discharge) and men (redness, irritation, or rash around the penis or scrotum).
Increased thirst and mild dehydration: Extra fluid loss can leave you feeling unusually thirsty.

Dehydration and low blood pressure: Can cause dizziness, lightheadedness, weakness, or fainting, especially when standing up. Risk is higher if you take water pills (diuretics), are over 65, or have kidney issues.

Diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA): A dangerous buildup of acid in the blood—which can happen even if your blood sugar is not very high. Symptoms include nausea, vomiting, stomach pain, unusual tiredness, trouble breathing, or a fruity odor on your breath.

Low blood sugar (Hypoglycemia): More likely if you take Jardiance along with other diabetes medications like insulin or sulfonylureas. Symptoms include shaking, sweating, fast heartbeat, confusion, and headache.
Severe urinary tract or kidney infections: Infections that spread to the kidneys or blood (pyelonephritis, urosepsis).

Necrotizing fasciitis (Fournier’s gangrene): A rare, life-threatening bacterial infection of the tissue under the skin in the perineum (area between the genitals and anus) causing severe pain, redness, swelling, and fever.
Lower limb amputations: An increased risk has been observed with SGLT2 inhibitors, particularly for people with a history of prior amputations, peripheral vascular disease, or diabetic foot ulcers.
Serious allergic reactions: Hives, or swelling of the face, lips, tongue, or throat causing trouble swallowing or breathing.

text_blocks.snippet: You can learn more details on the Boehringer Ingelheim Jardiance Site or review the drug details via the Mayo Clinic Empagliflozin Guide.
